round: 24b (audit 24, D M5; approved by the owner 22 October 2026)
decision: a label only, no number changes: countries with no real alternative to Russian fuel, the mirror of the 'gas cut off by Russia' label. 'Partly' where an alternative exists on paper but its capacity is officially contested (the Adria pipeline for Hungary and Slovakia).

criteria.C1_dependence: Russia >= 75% of the country's 2021 imports of the commodity (Comtrade HS 2709 / 2710 / 2711, or national data where Comtrade books transit countries) AND imports >= 50% of domestic consumption
criteria.C2_no_alternative: landlocked or pipeline-only for that commodity, AND either (a) every non-Russian route's usable capacity is < 50% of the country's imports of it in that year, or (b) the network and import monopoly is owned by a Russian state company (Gazprom-owned grid)
criteria.C3_period: label applies from 2022 until the first year an alternative meeting (a) is in service
criteria.partial: 'partly captive' when C1 holds and an alternative exists on paper but its capacity is officially contested (Adria for Hungary/Slovakia)
criteria.scope: label only; attaches to the negative 'paid' and 'windfall' parts for that commodity (like rusCut for 'cut by Russia'); totals unchanged

KGZ.c2: landlocked; EAEU duty-free Russian fuel; alternatives (Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, China) small; 2026 shortages when Russia restricted exports; its gas grid is owned by Gazprom Kyrgyzstan

ARM.c2: single pipeline via Georgia + Iran swap pipeline; Gazprom Armenia owns the network and the Armenian section of the Iran pipeline

SRB.c2: only route TurkStream via Bulgaria until the Bulgaria-Serbia interconnector (10 Dec 2023, 1.8 bcm = 60% of needs)

BIH.c1: all piped gas Russian via Serbia (Comtrade books 58% to Russia, rest to the transit country)

HUN.c2: Adria/JANAF: JANAF says 14.4 Mt/yr suffices; MOL disputes; EU embargo exempted pipeline crude for landlocked states

TJK.c2: rail routes via Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kazakhstan exist; no capacity constraint documented
